The code is IXGC. I found it by reading the weights only; I didn't run anything to test the network's play.

**Where it is:** the last four numbers of the first-layer bias `b1`, which belong to hidden units 28 to 31:

`b1[28..31] = 0.073, 0.088, 0.071, 0.067`

Multiply each by 1000 and you get 73, 88, 71, 67. Read as ASCII character codes, those are **I, X, G, C**.

**Why I think this is the hidden code and not chance:**
- The other biases are spread from about −0.45 to 0.65 with no pattern. Four values in a row all landing in the narrow capital-letter band (0.065 to 0.090) would be very unlikely by accident.
- Nothing else in the weights spells out letters the same way.

**What I ruled out:** a few hidden units have unusually clean, large weights. For example, unit 27 responds to the top row, unit 29 to the right column, unit 30 to the bottom row and unit 31 to the anti-diagonal. I checked whether these hid the code. They don't: each one fires when the mover has two pieces in its line and the third cell is empty, then pushes up that line's cells. Since only the empty cell can be played, the effect is to complete the winning line. That's ordinary learned tic-tac-toe behaviour, not a hidden message.

CODE: IXGC
